long_biography.plain_text:
During his career, Stanley S. Bey was working at Russell-Stanley Corporation, the New Jersey industrial-packaging company he later owned and led as chief executive. The business manufactured steel drums used to transport industrial products. Bey sold the company to an investor group in June 1989, ending his direct control of its operating platform.

A Monmouth alumnus, Bey also spent decades in university governance. He became the first graduate to chair the school's trustees and helped steer the successful effort that secured university status in 1995. Monmouth later named its business-school building Bey Hall for his parents, Samuel E. and Mollie Bey, and recognized him as its first graduate to contribute $1 million.
